2M likes, 7,342 comments - thefitnesschef_ on September 17, 2025: "Would you try this bizarre cheesy potato ‘thing’? Here’s how mine turned out 🥔 
-

I slightly modified mine to include mozzarella and chorizo. Additionally, instead of deep frying I used my air fryer.
-

Ingredients (makes 2):
600g peeled potatoes
2tbsp melted butter 
5tbsp flour
60g mozzarella 
30g chorizo
5ml olive oil
-

Method:
1. Peel and boil potatoes until soft, then drain and mash
2. Add the butter and flour and mix with a fork, and then your hands until smooth, then form a large ball with your hands 
3. Lay out a sheet of cling film, then drizzle the olive oil over it
4. Add the potato ball to the cling film and press to make a large circle
5. Add the mozzarella and chorizo to the centre of the circle
6. Use the cling film to roll up the potatoe on all 4 sides, pressing down and sealing any gaps
7. Air fryer at 240 degrees for 7-8 minutes each side, using a spatula to turn halfway
8. Once cooked, eating with a knife and fork is advised 🤣
-

Nutrition information per single serving:
-

Calories: 480
Protein: 20g
Carbs: 64g
Fat: 16g
-
Original recipe: @foodiefrontier0 
-

#recipeoftheday #potato #nutritionist".

628K likes, 2,029 comments - thefitnesschef_ on November 13, 2025: "Would you try these crispy ‘bang bang’ chicken tenders? 🍗💥 
-

Overall, these are exceptional on speed, crunch and taste. Here’s how to make them…
-

Ingredients:
Chicken:
300g chicken tenders (roughly 6)
1 egg
30g flour
50g cornflakes
1tsp garlic powder
1tsp onion powder
Salt & pepper
10 sprays cooking oil
-

Bang Bang Sauce:
100g 0% fat Greek yogurt
30g sweet chilli sauce
1 tsp sriracha 
20g honey 
5g extra sweet chilli sauce per tender
-

Method:
1. Season your chicken tenders with salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder.
2. In 3 separate bowls add an egg (whisked), flour and crushed cornflakes.
3. Dip each tender until coated into flour, then egg, then cornflakes. 
4. Add coated tenders to air fryer and add spray oil 
5. Air fry at 200 degrees C for 15 minutes
6. Meanwhile, in a small bowl add the sauce ingredients above and mix well with a spoon
7. Smear on extra sweet chilli sauce on each tender before dipping in the bang bang sauce.
-

Nutrition information per 3 fillets:
Calories: 477
Protein: 50g
Carbs: 58g
Fat: 5g
-

Original creator: @hunt4shredz 
-
#crispychicken #highprotein #nutrition".

16K likes, 147 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 26, 2026: "You need to try this sensational Crispy Chicken Parma Wrap 🌯

Ingredients:
150g chicken breast
1 large tortilla wrap
5ml olive oil 
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp Garlic powder
1 tsp Onion powder
1 tsp Chilli powder 
Salt
Pepper
Juice of 1/4 lemon
1/2 chopped onion
20g parmesan 
Fresh parsley
3 chopped iceberg lettuce leaves
Dipping sauce:
50g natural yogurt
1 tsp Dijon mustard
5g parmesan 
1/2 tsp smoked paprika
Juice of 1/4 lemon

Method:
1. Add the chicken breast, olive oil and seasoning to a large mixing bowl. Mix well with hands
2. Add to a non stick pan and cook for 3 mins
3. Add the Parmesan and onion and cook for further 7-8 mins
4. Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce by adding all ingredients and mixing thoroughly
5. Assemble the wrap by adding the lettuce to the centre, followed by the chicken, the folding 
6. Add to the same pan and crispen each side for 1-2 mins
7. Wrap bottom half of wrap in foil to hold together and serve

Nutrition information:
Calories: 524
Protein: 53g
Carbs: 42g
Fat: 16g
Fibre: 5g

Thanks to @iramsfoodstory for this outstanding recipe!

#recipeideas #fatloss #crispychicken".

20K likes, 1,044 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 22, 2026: "People think sugar is inherently bad - but it isn’t. It is simply an energy source without much nutritional value in the form of micronutrients and fibre.

When a food has healthful qualities it doesn’t mean everything about it is healthful. And when a food has less healthful qualities it doesn’t mean everything about it is unhealthful.

Sugar is still sugar, if it is presented in nutrient dense foods or not. Eventually all types of sugar are broken down to be the exact same molecule. It’s the micronutrients and fibre that provide health promoting qualities, not ‘better’ or ‘worse’ types of sugar.

When people claim they hardly eat any sugar, chances are they are eating more than they believe as it is often overlooked in foods that are deemed more nutrient dense.

When people demonize foods for being high in sugar, sometimes they aren’t as high as assumed when compared to more healthful foods.

It’s always better avoid making assumptions about the food you eat. Instead, being informed empowers you to make decisions that support your health and fitness goals. ✅

#sugar #diet #glucose".

16K likes, 292 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 21, 2026: "These plates of spaghetti bolognese appear identical as they have the exact same volume. 🍝

However, one plate contains 1000 calories and the other 635.

If you swap 200g of regular beef mince for the same quantity of 5% fat beef mince - you save 250 calories without losing volume or taste.

If you reduce the olive oil used from 20ml to 5ml - you save an additional 135 calories while still lubricating the pan.

These two extremely simple swaps reduce the plate by 385 calories to support a calorie deficit better.

Losing fat is not achieved through extreme actions. Instead, it is achieved by making adherence to a calorie deficit as easy as possible over long periods of time. ✅

#spaghetti #caloriedeficit #lowcalories".

27K likes, 384 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 18, 2026: "You are told obesity is caused by fast food, so-called junk food, insulin spikes from eating carbs, refined sugar, laziness and being a certain BMI.⁣⁣⁣⁣

But none of these things inherently cause obesity because many people eat all of the above and aren’t obese. And because many are classed as obese by their BMI, but only because they have lots of muscle mass.⁣⁣⁣⁣

What actually causes obesity is a combination of many underlying complexities. Food availability, social environments, work environments, social economics and mental health can all indirectly lead to one consistently consuming too many calories over a long period of time.⁣⁣⁣⁣

Instead of shaming, ridiculing and blaming people (and foods), understanding and empathizing with the underlying causes is how change can begin. It’s time for the government to stop wasting their time watching documentaries on TV designed for entertainment and wake up to what is actually happening.🫡✅⁣⁣

#obesity #nutrition #fitness".

41K likes, 1,021 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 15, 2026: "If you’re worried about the scale going up quickly after eating chocolate, donuts, pizza, cookies, ice cream, crisps, or any food you enjoy - this is what you’d actually need to eat to gain 1kg of body fat.

4 110g bars of diary milk
8 donuts
2 supermarket pizzas
4 cookies
Tub of Ben & Jerry’s
Huge packet of crisps 

It’s very unlikely you’d even eat a quarter of the above in a single day of high indulgence. If you see scale weight increase after eating some of the above, the probability is this is merely water weight.

For very gram of carbohydrate you consume your body retains 4g of water, which will disappear fairly quickly. The weight gain is not body fat.

No single food makes you gain body fat. Quantity, frequency, energy expenditure and overall lifestyle over long periods of time define how much body fat you have. 

#fatloss #snacking #nutritionist".

18K likes, 268 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 13, 2026: "Six chicken McNuggets, 1 low fat cheese, 150g blackberries and a square of dark chocolate contains more protein, fewer calories, more fibre and as many nutrients as a bottle of huel.

Did you know an entire pack of Oreos contains less sugar than 75g (a handful) of raisins? 

Did you know an iced donut contains 4 times more protein and fewer calories than 2 slim fast snack bars (which are incredibly small)?

Did you 150g baked beans contains more fibre than a fibre one bar?

Often, people will assume fast food, cheese, chocolate, oreos and donuts are bad, and huel, raisins, slimming bars and fibre one bars are good. But there are no good or bad foods in the context of your overall diet. 

When you actually look at the content of the food you eat and apply it to the context of everything you eat you are able to understand what a supportive food choice is. Knowledge dictates your choices, not marketing.

If your diet is nutrient dense and moderate in calories you can still enjoy any food you wish. You don’t need to pay large sums of money for products promising elite health when eating regular food does the same job, or on most occasions is actually more supportive. 🙏

#nutrition #dieting #fitnesslife".

13K likes, 103 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 12, 2026: "Here’s how to make this protein packed breakfast wrap 👀⬇️

Ingredients (serves 2)
20ml olive oil
200g thinly sliced potatoes
4 eggs, whisked 
2 slices tomatoes 
Tortilla wrap
60g grated mozzarella 
80g wafer ham

Method:
1. Add potatoes to boiling water and simmer for 10-15 mins to part boil, then set aside to cool before thinly slicing 
2. Add the olive oil to a preheated pan, then add the potato slices and fry each side for 2-3 mins until crispy 
3. Add the tomato slices on top of the potatoes before adding the whisked eggs, followed by the tortilla 
4. Using a spatula, gently fold over to flip the omelette 
5. Add the mozzarella and ham, gently folding over and cooking for a further 2-3 mins until the mozzarella melts 

Nutrition (per serving)
Calories: 498
Protein: 31g
Carbs: 44g
Fat: 22g

Original creator: @pembissunumlarim 

#breakfast #omelette #recipeoftheday".

44K likes, 226 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 5, 2026: "This high protein pulled lamb pasta salad needs to enter your life. 🥗 Here’s how to make it ⤴️

I slightly modified the quantities of ingredients to ensure each portion was higher in protein and lower in calories. Here’s the full recipe:

Ingredients (serves 2):
150g uncooked pasta
1 tbsp oregano
Salt & pepper
15ml olive oil
1 sliced red onion
1/2 chopped cucumber 
1/2 chopped red pepper
300g pulled lamb shoulder (most supermarkets offer precooked)
12 Kalamata olives 
75g tzatziki
Fresh dill
Fresh mint
75g crumbled feta

Method:
1. Add the pasta to a saucepan of boiling water and simmer for 6-8 mins until tender. Then rinse under cold water and drain.
2. Add the cooked pasta to a large mixing bowl, then add the oregano, salt, pepper, olive oil, red onion, red pepper, pulled lamb, Kalamata olives and tzatziki.
3. Mix thoroughly before topping with dill, mint and crumbled feta. Then serve!

Per portion:
Calories: 577
Protein: 42g
Carbs: 64g
Fat: 17g

Original recipe from: @poss.pantry 

#pasta #salad #worklunch".

22K likes, 753 comments - thefitnesschef_ on October 1, 2026: "What is actually in Diet Coke?🥤

Some of these ingredients sound scary. But it’s because we simply don’t know what they are. For example, caramel colouring is also sound in soy sauce. Sodium citrate is also found in jam and sports drinks. Both are harmless if consumed in moderation. Danger is in dose, not ingredient.

Aspartame is the most researched ingredient in history, and to this date there is no evidence that it inherently causes any harmful health outcomes.

People who say artificially sweetened drinks are bad for you are not consulting the body of evidence. 🙏

#dietcoke #fatloss #personaltrainer".
